pr_title: feat: Restrain sending http credentials on a specific origin
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/20464

Hi there.

For security purpose, we would like to restrain sending HTTP credentials to only the specified server. The idea is to give the ability to specify a origin (scheme://host:port) additionally to current pair username/password. When an authorization response is received from servers, the credentials are sent only if the server origin in the request matches case insensitive the specified origin.

If this PR is OK for you, we are also interested into improving the Java wrapper as a next step.

issue_context.title: [Feature] Restrain sending http credentials on a specific hostname
issue_context.body:
Let's consider doing a navigation on a page that requires HTTP authentication. From the browser, this would typically show a dialog prompting for user credentials.

With Playwright, this pair of string "username" and "password" can be set on the browser context with the code below: 

`const context = await browser.newContext({httpCredentials: { username: 'user', password: 'pass' }`

That allows Playwright to use these credentials when any servers respond with HTTP 401 unauthorized, in order to secure the connection. This works fine regardless of the HTTP authentication mecanism: basic, ntlm, kerberos...

However, we have a concern in terms of security, about these credentials being sent to any servers, other than the one we specified the credentials for. 

In order to restrain sending HTTP credential to only the expected server, we would like to have the ability to specify a hostname, additionaly to the current pair username/password set on the browser context. So when an authorization response is received from servers, the credentials are sent only if the server hostname in the request matches case insensitive the specified hostname. Otherwise, if the hostname does not match, then the credentials wouldn't be sent, same as if no credentials were configured (likely causing the server to fail the authorization and return 401 HTTP status). 

Also, in order to not break the compatibility with previous project, that additional parameter for the hostname needs to be optional. When not present, it should behave exactly the same way as before, namely always sending the credentials to any server.

We submitted a PR for that matter: #20374. We could also consider a more advance matching algorighm if you prefer (such as regexp on full request path), but we thought doing a simple string compare of the full hostname could be enough as a first step. Later, we are also interested into improving the Java wrapper.
comments: @SebastienRichert: looks like we need to use origin instead of the hostname as per @dgozman , please ack!
@pavelfeldman: Completely agree ! We'll update the PR to have the parameter "origin" as optional string (instead of hostname only.

review_comments: You don't need `&& this._credentials` check here

Yeah, I did not have it at first, but I ended up adding it because without it the lint check fails (even though the build work). My understanding was that on that line, this._credentials can be null, so in that case it cannot map the username and password from this._credentials to the const {username, password}.

Adding the `&& this._credentials` check here guarantee that if there are not credentials, it just goes to the `{ username: undefined, password: undefined };`

Technically it shoudn't happen, if there are no credential, the variable `shouldProvideCredentials` would be false anyway... Maybe there is a different syntax to achieve this ?
